reviewer: Specialist: life_safety, accessibility, acoustics_av (other disciplines not scored)
weighted_score_note: Weighted over the three assigned disciplines only (15/10/10, normalised to 35). Not comparable to a full nine-discipline score.

findings.finding: The two upper-foyer stairs that carry the rear 1,145 occupants down from +4.42 m are single straight flights of 26 risers with no intermediate landing, open to the foyer (not enclosed or protected).
findings.evidence: geometry_checks.json stairs ARC-STAIR-FOYER-W/E: run 9.0 m (y 2.6 to 11.6), width 5.4 m; metrics foyer_stair_risers 26, riser 0.170 (going about 0.36 m); EGR-02 rear_load_to_upper_foyer 1145; basis_of_design s.4 'rise through openings in the upper-foyer slab'.
findings.fix: Split each stair into two flights of 13 risers with a landing at least as deep as the stair is wide (a dog-leg, or a longer straight run with a mid landing). Add a central handrail on each 5.4 m stair. The fire engineer should decide whether the stairs and upper foyer need fire or smoke separation from the main foyer.

findings.finding: Travel distances exceed the placeholder flags. They are honestly logged, but they remain the main weakness of a 50 m wide end-stage hall: 330 occupants are over 30 m from the nearest exit (max 39.7 m), 490 are over 30 m with queue balancing (max 50.9 m), and the longest route to an external door is 61.6 m.
findings.evidence: geometry_checks.json EGR-03N {max 39.73, over_flag 330}, EGR-03 50.87, EGR-04 61.62 (WARN); open_issues.md OI-17 with a restriction on use.
findings.fix: Test vomitory exits under the rear rake at the +1.2 m cross aisle, or exits through the platform wings to the stage rear, then re-run EGR-03/03N. Keep the restriction on use until a fire engineer accepts a strategy.

findings.finding: If occupants take the shortest route to an external door, the two mid cross-aisle exits are overloaded (817 and 843 occupants against 3.36 m clear width). The queue-balanced assignment that passes is a heuristic, and occupants naturally favour these exits because they lead straight outside.
findings.evidence: exit_schedule.csv DR-HALL-W-CROSS / E-CROSS load_shortest_route_to_outside_sensitivity 817 / 843, check UNDER (needs 4.085 / 4.215 m); EGR-01R WARN.
findings.fix: Widen the cross-aisle exits (for example two 3.6 m door sets per side, or one 4.8 m set) or add a second exit per side on the cross aisle, then re-run EGR-01R.

findings.finding: The rear aisle steps use a 0.14 m riser with a 0.95 m going (one step per row), which gives an irregular stride on a busy egress route. The 1:11.18 front slope is steep for an aisle used in an evacuation.
findings.evidence: geometry_checks.json GEO-05 uniform_riser 0.14, metrics aisle_min_going 0.95; GEO-04 1:11.18; OI-06.
findings.fix: Rework the rear aisle steps with the architect: either a steeper rake with two equal steps per row, or aisle ramps no steeper than 1:12. Add nosing contrast and keep the step lights, which already exist as allowances.

findings.finding: The reports contain stale or inconsistent figures. OI-18 still describes the PL06 choir arrangement and a 0.90 m platform (now 1.00 m), and the basis of design gives the maximum eye distance as both 51.3 m and 44.5 m in the same section.
findings.evidence: open_issues.md OI-18; DESIGN_BRIEF PL07 (1.00 m); basis_of_design.md s.2 table vs Recommendation paragraph.
findings.fix: Regenerate OI-18 from PL08, and make the recommendation read the metric max_viewing_distance_to_platform_edge.

findings.finding: Wheelchair users have no place on the rear (+4.42) level, so the lift serves only the upper foyer and booth. Refuge on the open upper foyer is an allowance only, with no enclosure or communication.
findings.evidence: ACC-05 refuges 4, L02 wheelchair spaces 0; OI-16.
findings.fix: Keep the client decision, but design an enclosed refuge with two-way communication at each stair head, and size the lift as an evacuation lift if local code allows.

findings.finding: No wheelchair place is on the central axis near the front. The 24 mid-band places sit in one line at +1.2 m, and the 6 front places are at the hall-floor corners (x 7-11 m and 47-51 m).
findings.fix: Move two to four front places into the central blocks of rows 1-2 (level floor) so that some front positions face the pulpit directly.

findings.finding: The hall volume is very large for amplified worship (49,768 m3, or 16.6 m3 per seat), and the hall is a box whose rear wall runs parallel to the platform about 48 m away. Without heavy absorption the reverberation will be long, and the rear wall will send a late echo back to the platform about 280 ms after the direct sound.
findings.evidence: comparison.md hall air volume 49,768 m3, volume per seat 16.59; basis_of_design hall depth 48.0 m (grid 3-9); roof top +18.40; OI-09 (no acoustic analysis).
findings.fix: Commission an early RT estimate. Make the rear wall and the upper-foyer glazing absorptive or diffusive. Add a suspended absorptive or diffusing ceiling below the trusses, which also reduces the effective volume. Splay or diffuse the side walls.

findings.finding: Screen coverage passes SGT-H1, but 2,002 seats depend on screens. The delay screens and speakers hang over the middle of the hall at +9.4 to +11.6 m, and there is no check of vertical viewing angle or of trusses blocking the view. The main arrays (y 62.8) are about 45 m from the rear rows.
findings.evidence: geometry_checks.json SGT-H1 relying_on_screens 2002; auditorium_params.json av DELAY-* centre z 9.4, speakers DELAY-L/R z 11.6, MAIN-L/R y 62.8.
findings.fix: Add vertical viewing-angle limits (for example 30 deg to the screen centre) and a truss-obstruction ray check to SGT-H1. Ask the AV consultant to confirm the delay-ring timing and the rigging points.

findings.finding: The open front edge of the platform and the band area sit close to the main LED wall and main arrays, and the concept does not address microphone feedback or monitoring at the pulpit.
findings.evidence: auditorium_params.json av MAIN-L/R at y 62.8 vs platform front (PL07 platform against the rear wall).
findings.fix: Keep the main arrays forward of the pulpit microphone position, and record this as an AV design requirement.

strengths: There are 10 hall exits with 26.88 m effective clear width against a 17.54 m placeholder demand, and 23.52 m remains with the largest exit blocked (EGR-06).

The mid cross-aisle wheelchair band has a direct 1:12 outside ramp on both sides (ACC-06, 2 flights of 7.2 m), and the ambulatory ramps run at 1:12.62 to 1:14.13 with landings. This gives wheelchair users a genuinely step-free escape.
Only about a third of hall occupants (1,145) depend on stairs; the rest leave at grade or at +1.2 m with ramps.
Egress exceedances are reported as WARN with a restriction on use. No compliance is claimed.
Sightlines meet C >= 0.06 / 0.12 everywhere (SGT-01/02), no seat is more than 52 deg off the pulpit axis, and the deep rear zone has delay screens and speakers.
limitations: Distances come from the design's own plan engine and the shared comparison script; I did not re-derive every door position from the manifest matrices for A. I did not model the acoustics: RT and echo times are first-order estimates from volume and dimensions. Local Zimbabwean fire, accessibility and occupancy requirements were not available, so all widths, distances and riser limits are placeholders.
certification_disclaimer: This is a concept-stage QA review score. It is not professional certification, fire/egress approval, accessibility audit, acoustic design or code-compliance confirmation; a qualified fire engineer, access consultant and acoustician must review the design under applicable Zimbabwean requirements.
